messages:
sam (product): quick design check: org usage page — two contender layouts: 'scan-first' (more vertical spacing, large toolbar CTAs, explicit token-denom toggle top-right) vs 'dense-scan' (compact rows, token chips inline, row overflow). which should be org default? figma: https://figma.com/file/scanvden
indra (design): my vote: org = scan-first. Execs want readable rows and clear toolbar. dense-scan is useful for project pages where users need granular actions.
zara (frontend): perf note: dense rows + inline chips = many DOM nodes for big orgs. we can virtualize rows and lazy-load chip details. overflow-only per-row is cheaper.
pat (a11y): accessibility: small chips and icon-only row buttons fail keyboard hit-area rules. If we keep dense, ensure focus-reveal: on focus show text label. Toolbar download needs clear aria-description: "Downloads visible invoices".
mike (eng): backend: toolbar bulk-download must support batch job + job_id; we'll add /billing/export and job polling. Also suggest server-side batch zip to avoid many small requests.
anya (data): small prototype numbers: when row Download visible, click rate ~28%; toolbar-only ~11%. suggests discoverability matters. propose A/B: variant A = scan-first baseline, B = hybrid (scan-first default + visible per-row overflow). measure: downloads/user, support ticket start, page initial-paint ms.
infra-bot: batch_export_job queued id=job_771 org=org-xyz
sam (product): leaning hybrid: default = scan-first (org) but include lightweight overflow per-row (three dots) that exposes Download + View. project pages default to dense-scan. indra, can you mock overflow focus-expand? zara, will overflow reduce perf hit vs inline buttons?
zara (frontend): yes, overflow uses a single minimal button per row and fetches menu on open. much cheaper. will implement lazy hydrate and virtualization.
pat (a11y): ensure overflow menu has role=menu, arrow-key nav, and menu items have descriptive aria-labels (e.g., "Download invoice April 2026, $2,100"). also add ARIA-live toast for batch jobs.
sam (product): ok next steps: (1) indra post updated frames (~3h) (2) mike add endpoints + rate-limit plan (3) zara PR for lazy menus + virt v2 (4) anya AB dashboard + baseline. sync Fri 9:30. :white_check_mark:
